subject: Clarify: unexpected mid-cycle embed spike & EU VAT routing (OmniSoft)
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia@omnisoft.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@omnisoft.io>
Date: Thu, 06 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected spike on May 31 invoice — can you help?

Hi Neha,

We pulled the May invoice and saw a ~320% jump in embed token units on 2028-05-31 compared to normal. This pushed us into an overage tier and doubled the expected bill. We do a lot of nightly batch indexing, but nothing changed on our side — no new jobs were deployed.

Can Redwood share the raw usage samples for May 31 between 02:00–06:00 UTC? Also, we're an EU-registered subsidiary and need to confirm whether the excess will be routed to our EU billing entity (so VAT treatment stays consistent). Liam is copied for accounting.

We'd like to request a provisional credit while you investigate, if this looks like a meter/ingest duplication.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Director of Platform Ops, OmniSoft
---
Sent from my laptop

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@omnisoft.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 06 Jun 2028 12:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on May 31 invoice — can you help?

Hi Alicia — thanks for flagging this. I reviewed the high-level telemetry and attached a quick usage snapshot (usage_snapshot_2028-05-31.csv) showing per-minute token counts for your API keys.

Preliminary notes:
- There is a sharp spike at ~02:44 UTC (5/31) with repeated identical request fingerprints over ~18 minutes. That pattern usually indicates a retry loop from the client or a duplicate submission by the ingest worker.
- The requests were routed to our embed pipeline (gpt-embed-3b-quant) with an unusually high sequence length for that period.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Can your team confirm whether any of your nightly jobs retried around 02:40–03:05 UTC or if there were queue replays?
2) We'll pull the request-level trace (request ids + socket ids) and the retry trace on our side; I attached the initial log extract (retry-log-trace-2028-05-31.txt).

On VAT routing: the usage is currently billed against your primary account (US entity) in our ledger. If this was legitimately generated by your EU subsidiary's keys, we can reassign these tokens to the EU entity and reissue an invoice with reverse-charge VAT handling — but we'll need a formal claim and some supporting evidence (owner of API keys / HubSpot deal reference).

I'm looping in Ben and Kim from Billing to propose a provisional credit while we confirm the root cause. If this was a duplication on our side, we'll credit the full overage. If it's from a customer-side retry, we'll work through a partial credit.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: usage_snapshot_2028-05-31.csv; retry-log-trace-2028-05-31.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Unexpected spike on May 31 invoice — provisional credit proposal

Neha / Kim — quick read on my side after seeing the traces Neha attached.

Summary:
- The request fingerprints show identical payload IDs and identical mid-request KV states repeated ~26 times; the pattern looks like an exponential client retry (5 retries per failed chunk).
- On our infrastructure side, the routing was normal and there were no simultaneous duplicate worker launches that would have caused double-counting.

Recommendation:
1) Offer OmniSoft a provisional credit equal to the incremental overage from the spike period (I estimate ~€7,400 based on their rateband).
2) Ask for confirmation from their infra team about the retry loop; if they confirm the retry-origin, offer a one-time remediation credit of 50% and provide guidance on idempotency headers to prevent repeat behavior.
3) For VAT: if OmniSoft can confirm these tokens belong to the EU subsidiary (we need the EU account id and VAT number), reassign usage to the EU entity and reissue corrected invoice with reverse-charge. Otherwise, leave the ledger as-is and treat the credit as a billing adjustment.

Kim — can you own the credit paperwork and tax routing (reissue invoice or credit note)? I'll approve provisional amount so we can unblock collections hold.

Ben Carter
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@omnisoft.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Jun 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on May 31 invoice — proposed provisional credit & next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks for your patience. Based on the traces and Neha's attachments, Redwood is prepared to issue a provisional credit while the root cause is finalized. Proposed steps: 

1) Provisional credit: we will apply a provisional credit of €7,400 to your account (visible as a negative line on next invoice) effective immediately. This will prevent collections action while we close the investigation.

2) Evidence & VAT routing: to reassign the tokens to your EU subsidiary and reissue the invoice under reverse-charge, please reply with the EU entity's legal name and VAT number and confirm which API key(s) belong to that entity. Once we have that, we will reassign the usage in our ledger and generate a corrected invoice.

3) Credit paperwork: attached is the provisional credit note (provisional-credit-note.pdf). We can finalize this via DocuSign — I included a link to the agreement.

4) Technical guidance: Neha's team recommends ensuring idempotency keys on batched uploads and adding a short jitter/linear backoff on retries. Our engineering notes are attached for your ops team.

Please confirm receipt and whether OmniSoft accepts the provisional credit and will provide the EU VAT info. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute troubleshooting call this week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Accounting Manager, Redwood Inference
